body: If you are comparing **Claude Code vs OpenHands**, the short answer is: Choose Claude Code for a commercial terminal coding agent; choose OpenHands for open-source repository automation experiments.
This comparison focuses on adoption fit rather than hype. The better tool is the one that matches your workflow surface, review process, and risk tolerance.
## Fast answer
| Question | Better fit | Why |
| Need terminal coding agent for Anthropic-centered development workflows? | [Claude Code](/agents/claude-code) | It is designed around that surface |
| Need open-source software engineering agent for repository tasks? | [OpenHands](/agents/openhands) | It optimizes for a different workflow shape |
| Need a first evaluation? | Start with the narrower workflow | Small tests reveal failure modes faster than broad demos |
## Core difference

[Claude Code](/agents/claude-code) is best understood as terminal coding agent for Anthropic-centered development workflows. [OpenHands](/agents/openhands) is best understood as open-source software engineering agent for repository tasks. That difference matters because both tools may be called AI agents, but they usually operate at different layers of the stack.

A good Claude Code vs OpenHands decision should begin with the work surface. Are you trying to edit code, operate a browser, orchestrate multiple agents, run local models, evaluate outputs, or preserve memory? Once that surface is clear, the choice becomes less abstract.
## When to choose Claude Code

Choose [Claude Code](/agents/claude-code) when your primary need aligns with terminal coding agent for Anthropic-centered development workflows. It is the better starting point if your first experiment can be expressed in its native workflow rather than forced into another tool's interface.
The main evaluation question is not whether Claude Code can do everything. It is whether it gives you enough control, logs, and repeatability for the task you actually want to run.
## When to choose OpenHands

Choose [OpenHands](/agents/openhands) when your primary need aligns with open-source software engineering agent for repository tasks. It may be the better option if your team already works in the environment or architecture it assumes.
The tradeoff is that a better fit for one workflow can be a worse fit for another. Do not treat OpenHands as a drop-in replacement for Claude Code unless the action surface is genuinely similar.
## Comparison table
| Criteria | Claude Code | OpenHands |
| Primary fit | terminal coding agent for Anthropic-centered development workflows | open-source software engineering agent for repository tasks |
| Best first test | One narrow workflow with clear pass/fail criteria | One narrow workflow with clear pass/fail criteria |
| Review model | Inspect outputs, logs, diffs, or traces before expanding access | Inspect outputs, logs, diffs, or traces before expanding access |
| Main risk | Assuming a demo generalizes to production | Assuming a demo generalizes to production |
| Adoption advice | Start with a sandbox | Start with a sandbox |
## Practical recommendation
Choose Claude Code for a commercial terminal coding agent; choose OpenHands for open-source repository automation experiments.

If your team is still unsure, run both tools against the same small task. Keep the task boring: one repository issue, one browser flow, one document set, one local model endpoint, or one evaluation suite. The winner is the tool that produces the most reviewable result with the least operational surprise.

## FAQ
### Is Claude Code better than OpenHands?
Not universally. Choose Claude Code for a commercial terminal coding agent; choose OpenHands for open-source repository automation experiments.
### Can Claude Code and OpenHands be used together?
Sometimes, but prove the simple version first. Combining tools too early can make failures harder to diagnose.
### What should I measure in a comparison?
Measure task completion, reviewability, setup time, permission control, repeatability, and recovery from failure. Those signals matter more than a polished demo.
### Which one is better for production?
The production answer depends on governance. Prefer the option that supports sandboxing, narrow permissions, audit trails, and a human review loop for your specific workflow.
